detail.why_not_a_partial_attempt: 004's own argument is that its four items are one commit, because one pin blocks all of them and one revision bump releases all of them. Doing A, B and D without C would spend revision 2 on a pass carrying degraded: ["librarian_agent"] and force the librarian run into revision 3 -- which is the 'four revisions of a question nobody has run' the card refuses. tasks/000 is more direct still: revision 2 IS the librarian run, not a save. A degraded revision 2 would be a revision that misrepresents what it is.
detail.what_this_adds_to_the_two_bridge_rows: this is the third instance and the first outside bridge/, so the cause is not bridge-specific. It also settles the one piece the bridge row at 2026-09-20T02:50:35Z offered as an untestable hypothesis, from inside this seat's own boundary and without reading another agent's directory: ALLOWED_PATHS in contracts/validate.py anchors .mcp.json to the repository root alone -- r"^(plan.md|CLAUDE.md|ARCHITECT.md|README.md|.gitignore|.mcp.json)$" -- so a per-agent .mcp.json is refused by check 13 rather than merely untried. tasks/000 records the historical instance: a red check 13 on microscope_agent/.mcp.json, since removed. So the obvious fix is currently barred by the gate.
detail.what_would_not_fix_it: rooting a simulation window at the repository root. Two reasons, the second specific to this agent. CLAUDE.md reads a root cwd as a top-tier seat -- specify, do not implement -- so such a window is not this seat at all. And this agent's .claude/settings.json states its denials as relative patterns: envelope/safety.json, approvals/**, inbox/**. From simulation_agent/ those resolve and guard the three paths inside this tree that are not this seat's; from the repository root they resolve to paths that do not exist. CLAUDE.md says the outward denials are inert from here; moving the root inverts that and makes the inward ones inert, dropping the guards on the person-only envelope and approvals and on the bridge-only inbox.
detail.who_fixes: the person, with manager-simulation and the architecture seat. A seat cannot register an MCP server for its own window from inside it, and where a per-agent registration may live is an ALLOWED_PATHS and section 7 question, which is not an execution seat's to answer.

It reads 'a bead lot specification replaces this with an E3 value', which names a DOCUMENT that would arrive rather than a STATE that would obtain. A direct measurement satisfied the underlying condition by a better route -- E2, above the E3 the falsifier anticipated -- and the falsifier had nothing to match. Same defect 002 diagnoses in a_target one step milder: a_target's falsifier says when somebody would change their mind, a_sample's says which piece of paper would settle it, and both describe a route instead of a state. 'A measured or specified size at E3 or better exists' would have fired on either route. And a_sample does not survive re-grading: its numbers list is exactly ['bead_diameter'], so once that number stops being assumed the assumption has no numbers left, which is a deletion and not an edit -- which is what carries 11-2's unit from seven rationales to six.

detail.why_it_is_a_deviation: 6.2 rule 3 says contracts/ is read by everyone and written by nobody, and that another agent's directory is neither read nor written. The bridge exception runs the other way. Self-reported, following the precedent the rule itself records: a bridge seat read librarian_agent/src/ on 2026-09-19 diagnosing caller_id and reported itself.
detail.the_rule_s_own_test_applied: The test is not whether harm followed but whether the conclusion was reachable inside the boundary. Taken one at a time: (1) queries/log.jsonl, to confirm no line exists under the six caller_ids -- REACHABLE, and so a pure loss. 003 had already checked it, and check 45's own output says degraded cards are out of scope, so the validator was telling me the answer while I opened the log to re-confirm it. (2) the two failures.jsonl, to place this session's MCP absence against the bridge's -- SPLIT. The finding itself stands entirely on this tree plus contracts/: session_connectors_status has no librarian row, and ALLOWED_PATHS anchors .mcp.json to the repository root. What was NOT reachable is that the bridge had already hit it twice, which is what let me call it a pattern rather than a launch. (3) the repository-wide greps, for bead_diameter carriers and for what still cites target_decade_resolution -- MOSTLY REACHABLE for the parts that matter to this agent, since both questions are about this question's own cards; the scans crossed because they were written as repo-wide sweeps when the answer needed one directory.
detail.what_the_split_case_means: 6.2 rule 3 was amended on 2026-09-19 for exactly this shape: when something is not reachable inside the boundary, that is a CONTRACT DEFECT REPORT and not a licence to read. So the correct move on the pattern question was to report that no seat can see another seat's abandoned attempts, and let the contract gain somewhere that fact lives -- not to open bridge/failures.jsonl and find out. The peer coordination that followed makes this concrete: the same facts reached me by cross-session message anyway, which is the channel 6.2 rule 2 allows, and the message left no trace until this row.
detail.what_does_NOT_excuse_it: that manager-librarian messaged this seat first, and that 4.3.2 requires this seat to read librarian_agent/kb/exports/. That export read is authorised by name and is not part of this report; so is librarian_agent/kb/index.json, which this agent's own src/fanout.py reads as the pin source. A licence naming two paths does not extend to the tree those paths sit in, and the reads listed above were not on it.
detail.harm: none found. No write crossed a boundary, the three commits from this seat (b5e4cbb, f975432, 6574369) touch simulation_agent/ only, and the gate listed every other session's differing path as not checked. The cost is the one the rule names: a boundary that holds only when it is convenient is not a boundary, and this seat found it convenient twice in one session.
detail.what_would_have_caught_it: nothing. Denials are on Write and Edit, check 53 refuses a deny entry that would block reading, and the gate reads the tree a commit would create -- which is clean here. This closes by habit, like the shared-index hunk rule in 6.2, and 6.2's own note on that rule records it surviving under an hour between the two seats that wrote it.

detail.the_actual_cause: mcpjson servers are enabled PER SESSION by the person, and a newly opened session does not inherit the approval. manager-librarian read ~/.claude.json this morning and found enabledMcpjsonServers empty for all seven project paths; after the person approved, the librarian attached to that seat and to the microscope's, and not to sessions opened later. So the root .mcp.json being the only one in the tree is true and is NOT what blocks this seat -- the file is found, the server is simply not enabled for this window.
detail.what_this_retires: the ALLOWED_PATHS branch as a FIX. It stays true as a fact -- .mcp.json is anchored to the repository root, so a per-agent file is refused by check 13 -- and it is worth keeping because it forecloses the workaround somebody would otherwise try. It is just not the repair. The repair is one approval per session, by the person, and nothing else.
detail.what_makes_it_expensive: the failure is silent at the session level. A seat with no librarian tools gets no error; it proceeds on the degraded path, which for this agent is a legitimate way to finish, so a quiet day looks like an ordinary one. This agent's own CLAUDE.md says as much in as many words -- the independence that makes this agent worth running separately is what makes a missing round easy to miss here -- and the same property hides a missing service.
detail.what_is_NOT_silent: the cards. Session 1 made the degraded claim structural: cards.evidence defaults to degraded and clears only when a reply names the server, so a card produced in a session like this one labels itself, and check 45 reads the claim against the query log from the other side. So the damage a silent service can do is a seat that idles or proceeds degraded -- not a card that falsely says the librarian answered. That bound is worth stating, because it is the reason this row is a scheduling problem and not an evidence problem.
detail.who_fixes: the person, per session, at session start. Not this seat, not the manager, and not a contract change. A seat cannot enable a server for its own window from inside it, and it must not try.

Three sessions across two agents recorded this symptom, one of them read the user's own config, and none of them could see the one file that contained an explicit refusal -- because the file is excluded from version control by a rule outside the repository. 2.1 rule 9's shape again: the protection was documented and the door beside it was one nobody could look at.
